trickyParts: The compared surface is the live pod's spec.serviceAccountName, not the Sandbox's stored template: the API server leaves that field as written, unlike the reservations GKE Autopilot rewrites, which is why templateResized reads the template instead.

"" is read as default on both sides. The daemon writes "" into the template when service_account is unset (config's optionalString) while the API server stores "default" on the pod, so comparing either raw would read every pod of a deployment that names no account as drifted and replace the whole fleet at the first launch or sweep.

The account term sits outside the !installing guard that image drift has. A plugin install cannot change the account a pod was created with, so a pod on the wrong account is replaced whatever the launch is installing; the existing 'if installing && replace { l.spec.Plugins = nil }' then clears the install with no edit.

The image warning line had to stay byte-identical: watch_test.go counts its prefix and docs/kubernetes.md quotes it. The account warning is a second log line, so a pod holding both drifts is named twice.
Regenerating testdata/golden/root-operator-route.json with -update, never by hand: a hand edit passes the eye and fails TestOperatorRouteGolden. The one line it moved is serviceAccountName.
bun install rewrites bun.lock in this workspace (three workspace versions), so every install here was bun install --frozen-lockfile and jj status was read before each commit.
deviations: S1 (recorded in the plan): R1 says the pod's replacement 'keeps its Sandbox and disk'. The Sandbox is kept; an issue pod's disk is a generic ephemeral volume created and deleted with the pod (podkind.go, manifest.go), so it goes, exactly as it goes for image drift today. The controller's claim and a cache's volume do survive. No acceptance line changes, and the cost is written into docs/kubernetes.md's list of what ends an issue pod's disk.
S2 (recorded in the plan): R6 names two docs sections; three are edited. docs/kubernetes.md's 'What ends an issue pod's disk' is a third list of what replaces a pod and would otherwise be false.
